chapter: Tape one: clubs, musicians and old friends
title: Fazola's name, Buck Banner and Louis Armstrong's trumpet
summary: Lala says he gave Irving Fazola his name, speaks of his uncle Buck Banner, who has the gold-plated trumpet linked to Louis Armstrong, and old rotary-valve trumpets.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Everybody thought that was Irving's name. I gave Irving that name, Pasola. You know, when he was learning, when he was learning, you know, I told him, I said, now you go play with the tagging band, the De'Go band, twice a week, every voice. Go play with them, give band experience, I told him. Go play with the Pasola band. That's that thing, a little, a little, a little, a little, uh, him and, uh, what is what De'Go's name? Lucas Kiro? Yeah. They would go and play with him, you know, and everything. And Pete Bacopa I believe started too. Luke Skiro. He died. Yeah, Pete. He died. He died.
He died? Oh yeah. But Lucas Kiro? Yeah, he comes around. He's the one who used to play down at that, uh... American Legion. Yeah, Buck Banner. Something about Fred Dodd. Yeah, with Banner.
Uncle Buck, you know. Yeah. Buck Banner was my uncle. Is Buck still around?
I haven't seen it either. What'd you say, John? I think so. What was that call that used to play piano? Buck Banner. His uncle. Yeah. He married to my aunt. Yeah. He married to my aunt.
He married to my aunt. Yeah? Yeah, Buck's.
What about Red Dingman? Red Dingman.
Red died? I think so. I don't know.

I haven't seen any of them. Well, Rick, uh... Buck Banner got a trumpet. The Harrow B. J. trumpet that the Harrow B. J. gave me. Louis Armstrong brought me there and it made me a Fred with a trumpet. You know, they used to have a rotary valve on too, didn't you, Johnny? Someone said that. What? The one that you played for. Oh, that's Italian. I know I never really had one like that. No. What, they have strings on it?

Like a Fred's on it? No, like spoons. Yeah. So he was connected with a string. Nice string. It's a cat guy mostly. Yeah. No, no. It didn't work that way? The valve, the car trumpet was black. Yeah. And you played like this and you worked like this. They're pretty same.
I had black. Some of them connected up with metal, little metal.
